headline: 4 things
body: Ranked by how much evidence is actually behind them.
punch: Number 1 isn't the one people argue about.

headline: Number 4
body: Methylphenidate promoted premature growth plate closure in cell culture, and a 410 patient study found reduced weight and a temporary growth halt. Real signal, size not settled.
punch: Do not stop prescribed medication over this. Talk to the prescriber.

headline: Number 3
body: Obesity drives high insulin, and insulin appears to raise aromatase expression inside growth plate cartilage. More local aromatase means more local estrogen at the closure switch.
punch: Heavier kids are often tall early and not tall finally.

headline: Number 2
body: Testosterone and its derivatives raise growth velocity and skeletal maturation at the same time. Part of every androgen aromatises into estrogen, which is the closure signal.
punch: You grow faster and you close sooner. Same hormone.

headline: Number 1
body: It's not close. A man with a broken estrogen receptor never stopped growing. A man who couldn't make estrogen had open plates at adulthood. Block aromatase in boys and maturation slows.
punch: Everything else on this list works by feeding into this one.

headline: Notice the pattern
body: Three of the four converge on the same enzyme and the same hormone. This isn't four separate problems, it's one mechanism with several inputs.
punch: One switch. Multiple hands on it.

headline: Which is why
body: Ranking things separately implies they're independent. They're not. Fixing number 3 changes number 1, because that's the pathway it runs through.
punch: The ranking is useful. The separation is fake.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
